add.title: Thailand Separates LGBTQ Inmates, Considers Segregated Prison (NBC News/AP)
add.summary: NBC News/AP (29 Jan 2017): the Thai Department of Corrections says LGBT prisoners have been separated from other inmates nationwide since 1993; at Pattaya Remand Prison transgender inmates are held in a dedicated block apart from cisgender men. Trans woman Theerayut Charoenpakdee, stopped by police and expecting to be 'thrown in prison with all the men because I still have the title of Mr.,' was instead held in the separated wing. The government was also discussing what could be the world's first exclusively-LGBTQ prison facility (the Min Buri pilot), while accepting that transgender women elsewhere usually face a choice of men's cells or solitary. Of roughly 300,000 Thai prisoners, more than 6,000 were registered as sexual minorities.

add.title: Exclusion or protection? Activists skeptical about LGBT prison (Coconuts Bangkok)
add.summary: Coconuts Bangkok (30 Aug 2016): trans activist Nachacha Kongudom, arrested in June 2015 while protesting the junta, was sent to a men's prison against her request for a women's facility; prison officials told her that under Thai law 'she remains a man' and no Thai document can identify a trans woman as female, and during intake she was harassed and ordered to expose her body. The Department of Corrections then announced a pilot using Bangkok's Min Buri prison as an LGBT facility to prevent abuse of trans inmates, after Pattaya men's prison had already begun separating trans prisoners from cis men following reports of abuse. DOC figures: ~4,448 of ~300,000 prisoners identified as LGBT, 34 of them transgender. Activists welcomed the pilot but feared it 'could encourage exclusion' and insisted placement 'should be an option, not an obligation.'
